name: Flyweight
intent: Save memory by sharing the heavy, unchanging part of many similar objects instead of copying it into each one.
scenario: A forest has thousands of trees. Each tree has its own position, but trees of one species share the same name, colour and big texture.
problem: Each Tree object stores its position and also a copy of its species data, including a large texture. Ten thousand trees mean ten thousand copies of the same texture, and the program runs out of memory.
solution: Split each tree into intrinsic state (species data, shared and immutable) and extrinsic state (position, unique). Put the shared part in a TreeType flyweight created through a factory that caches by species. Each Tree keeps only its coordinates plus a reference to the shared TreeType.
pain: Every Tree carries its own copy of species name, colour and texture
10,000 trees means 10,000 copies of the same big texture
Memory grows with the number of trees, not the number of species
Changing a species' colour means updating every tree
benefits: One TreeType per species, shared by every tree of that species
Memory grows with species count plus tiny per-tree coordinates
Species data is updated in one place
whenToUse: You create a huge number of similar objects and memory is a real constraint
Much of each object's state can be made immutable and shared
Objects can be told their unique state when used, instead of storing it
whenNotToUse: You only have a few objects: sharing buys nothing
There is little state to share
Profiling has not shown memory to be a problem: this pattern adds complexity
pitfalls: Shared state must be immutable, or one change affects every user of it
Splitting intrinsic and extrinsic state makes code harder to read
The factory cache is shared global state
Trades memory for CPU: extrinsic state is passed around on every call

roles.label: Flyweight
roles.description: Immutable shared object holding intrinsic state.

roles.label: Flyweight Factory
roles.description: Creates flyweights and reuses existing ones.

roles.label: Context
roles.description: Holds the unique extrinsic state plus a flyweight reference.

quiz.question: A game has 50,000 particles. Each holds x, y, velocity and its own copy of a 200 KB sprite bitmap, and there are only 5 distinct sprites. The game runs out of memory. What should be shared?
options: The 5 sprite bitmaps, held by shared objects, while each particle keeps its own x, y and velocity
The x, y and velocity values, kept in one array that all 50,000 particles read from
The 50,000 particle objects, handed out from a pool to avoid creating new ones
The bitmaps only after compressing each copy, with each particle owning its compressed data
quiz.explanation: The big, identical, unchanging data (the sprite) is the intrinsic state to share, so 5 bitmaps replace 50,000. Position and velocity differ per particle, so they cannot be shared. Object pooling saves allocations but each pooled particle still carries its bitmap.

quiz.question: In a forest renderer, 10,000 trees share one TreeType object for each species. A developer adds a method that sets the leaf colour to red, to show one tree on fire, and it changes the TreeType. What happens?
options: Every tree of that species turns red, so the colour should be extrinsic state passed in when drawing
The factory detects the change and creates a new TreeType for the one tree that was altered
Only the burning tree changes, because each tree owns a private reference to the TreeType
Every tree of every species turns red, because the factory cache is one shared global object
quiz.explanation: All trees of a species point to the same object, so changing it changes all of them. Shared state has to be immutable, and per-tree values such as the fire effect belong in extrinsic state. A factory does not copy on write by itself.

quiz.question: A text editor shares a flyweight per (font family, size, colour) for each character. Users may pick any of 16 million colours per character. In one 1M-character document the factory holds 900,000 flyweights. What is the best fix?
options: Keep colour in the flyweight key but hash the colours into 256 buckets to cut the key space
Remove the factory and create a new flyweight object for each character to avoid cache cost
Take colour out of the shared key and pass it as extrinsic state when drawing, keeping family and size shared
Add an LRU eviction rule to the factory so the cache stays at a fixed number of entries
quiz.explanation: The sharing ratio is almost 1, because nearly every key is unique. The value that varies most is not worth sharing, so it should be extrinsic. Eviction only hides the symptom, and bucketing colours would change what users see.
